concept.title: When to use JSON editor
concept.shortdesc: Use JSON editor for exact raw review, migration checks, troubleshooting, and values that are easier to handle as raw policies.json.

conbody.p: JSON editor is powerful but less guided than the visual editors. It should be a deliberate choice when the user needs boundary-document precision.

section.title: Good fit
section.p: Use JSON editor for exact policies.json review, migration checks, raw fallback values, or troubleshooting malformed import/export documents.

section.title: Not the first choice
section.p: Use Guided editor for common workflows and All settings for full visual inspection before choosing raw JSON for routine edits.

section.title: Validation boundary
section.p: Valid JSON syntax is not enough. BPM also validates Firefox policy values, schema channel support, and the canonical normalized model before save.

section.title: Examples
section.p: A valid example keeps a top-level policies object with entries such as DisableTelemetry and Preferences, including a locked browser.startup.homepage value. Invalid examples include malformed JSON syntax and schema-invalid policy values such as a string where a boolean is required.
